concepts.name: Points, Lines, and Planes
concepts.description: Undefined terms in geometry: a point has no dimension, a line has one dimension extending infinitely in both directions, and a plane has two dimensions extending infinitely. Collinear points lie on the same line; coplanar points lie in the same plane. Naming conventions using letters and notation.

concepts.name: Line Segments, Rays, and Measurement
concepts.description: A line segment has two endpoints and a definite length. A ray has one endpoint and extends infinitely in one direction. Measuring and comparing segment lengths. The midpoint of a segment and the segment addition postulate.

concepts.name: Angles: Definition and Measurement
concepts.description: An angle is formed by two rays with a common endpoint (vertex). Measuring angles in degrees using a protractor. Classifying angles as acute (< 90°), right (= 90°), obtuse (90° < x < 180°), and straight (= 180°). The angle addition postulate.

concepts.name: Angle Pairs and Relationships
concepts.description: Complementary angles sum to 90°; supplementary angles sum to 180°. Vertical angles are formed by two intersecting lines and are congruent. Adjacent angles share a vertex and a side. Linear pairs of angles are supplementary.

concepts.name: Parallel Lines and Transversals
concepts.description: When a transversal crosses parallel lines, corresponding angles are congruent, alternate interior angles are congruent, alternate exterior angles are congruent, and co-interior (same-side interior) angles are supplementary. Using these relationships to find angle measures.

concepts.name: Triangle Properties
concepts.description: Classifying triangles by sides (scalene, isosceles, equilateral) and by angles (acute, right, obtuse). The triangle angle-sum theorem: the interior angles of any triangle sum to 180°. The exterior angle theorem.

concepts.name: Congruent Triangles
concepts.description: Two triangles are congruent if all corresponding sides and angles are equal. Congruence criteria: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, and HL (for right triangles). Writing congruence statements with correct correspondence. Using CPCTC (Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent).

concepts.name: Isosceles and Equilateral Triangle Theorems
concepts.description: The isosceles triangle theorem: base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent. The converse: if two angles of a triangle are congruent, the opposite sides are congruent. Equilateral triangles are equiangular (all angles are 60°).

concepts.name: Triangle Inequality and Side-Angle Relationships
concepts.description: The triangle inequality theorem: the sum of any two side lengths must be greater than the third. The side-angle relationship: the longest side is opposite the largest angle. Using these to determine possible triangle dimensions.

concepts.name: Triangle Midsegment Theorem
concepts.description: The midsegment connecting the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half its length. Applications: finding segment lengths and verifying parallel segments in triangles.

concepts.name: Similar Triangles
concepts.description: Two triangles are similar if corresponding angles are congruent and corresponding sides are proportional. Similarity criteria: AA, SAS~, SSS~. Setting up and solving proportions from similar triangles. Scale factor.

concepts.name: Pythagorean Theorem
concepts.description: In a right triangle, a² + b² = c² where c is the hypotenuse. Using the theorem to find a missing side length. The converse: if a² + b² = c², the triangle is right-angled. Pythagorean triples (3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17).

concepts.name: Special Right Triangles
concepts.description: The 45-45-90 triangle: legs are congruent and the hypotenuse is √2 times a leg. The 30-60-90 triangle: hypotenuse is twice the shorter leg; longer leg is √3 times the shorter leg. Using these patterns to find exact side lengths without a calculator.

concepts.name: Right Triangle Trigonometry: Sine, Cosine, Tangent
concepts.description: SOH-CAH-TOA: sine = opposite/hypotenuse, cosine = adjacent/hypotenuse, tangent = opposite/adjacent. Using trigonometric ratios to find missing side lengths and angle measures in right triangles. Inverse trigonometric functions (arcsin, arccos, arctan).

concepts.name: Properties of Quadrilaterals
concepts.description: Classifying quadrilaterals: trapezoid, parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus, and square. Properties of each: parallel sides, congruent sides, right angles, congruent diagonals, bisecting diagonals, perpendicular diagonals. Hierarchy of quadrilaterals.

concepts.name: Parallelogram Theorems
concepts.description: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are congruent and parallel, opposite angles are congruent, consecutive angles are supplementary, and diagonals bisect each other. The converse theorems for proving a quadrilateral is a parallelogram.

concepts.name: Perimeter and Area of Triangles
concepts.description: Perimeter of a triangle: sum of side lengths. Area of a triangle: A = ½bh where b is the base and h is the corresponding height. Finding the area given side lengths and the included angle using A = ½ab·sin(C). Heron's formula for area given three side lengths.

concepts.name: Perimeter and Area of Quadrilaterals
concepts.description: Area formulas for parallelogram (A = bh), rectangle (A = lw), triangle (A = ½bh), trapezoid (A = ½(b₁+b₂)h), and rhombus/square (A = ½d₁d₂). Choosing the correct formula given available information. Composite figures.

concepts.name: Circles: Definitions and Parts
concepts.description: A circle is the set of all points equidistant from the center. Vocabulary: radius, diameter, chord, secant, tangent, arc (major/minor), sector, central angle, inscribed angle. Relationship between diameter and radius (d = 2r).

concepts.name: Circumference and Area of a Circle
concepts.description: Circumference: C = 2πr = πd. Area: A = πr². Arc length: (θ/360) × 2πr for a central angle θ in degrees. Sector area: (θ/360) × πr². Using these formulas to solve real-world problems.

concepts.name: Circle Theorems: Arcs, Chords, and Angles
concepts.description: A central angle equals its intercepted arc. An inscribed angle equals half its intercepted arc. A tangent-chord angle equals half the intercepted arc. Chord relationships: if two chords intersect inside a circle, the products of their segments are equal.

concepts.name: Distance and Midpoint Formulas
concepts.description: Distance between two points: d = √[(x₂-x₁)² + (y₂-y₁)²] (derived from the Pythagorean theorem). Midpoint formula: M = ((x₁+x₂)/2, (y₁+y₂)/2). Applications: finding perimeters, classifying figures on a coordinate plane.

concepts.name: Coordinate Proofs
concepts.description: Proving geometric theorems using coordinates. Strategically placing figures on a coordinate plane (e.g., a rectangle with vertices at (0,0), (a,0), (0,b), (a,b)). Using distance, midpoint, and slope to verify properties such as congruence, parallelism, and perpendicularity.

concepts.name: Equation of a Circle
concepts.description: Standard form of a circle: (x - h)² + (y - k)² = r² where (h, k) is the center and r is the radius. Writing the equation given center and radius. Finding center and radius from the equation. Completing the square to convert general form to standard form.

concepts.name: Surface Area and Volume of Prisms and Cylinders
concepts.description: Lateral area and total surface area of prisms (SA = 2B + Ph) and cylinders (SA = 2πr² + 2πrh). Volume of prisms (V = Bh) and cylinders (V = πr²h). B is the base area and h is the height.

concepts.name: Surface Area and Volume of Pyramids and Cones
concepts.description: Lateral area and total surface area of regular pyramids (SA = B + ½Pl, where l = slant height) and cones (SA = πr² + πrl). Volume of pyramids and cones: V = ⅓Bh. The relationship V(pyramid) = ⅓ × V(prism with same base and height).

concepts.name: Surface Area and Volume of Spheres
concepts.description: Surface area of a sphere: SA = 4πr². Volume of a sphere: V = (4/3)πr³. Applying these formulas to solve problems. Composite solids involving hemispheres.

concepts.name: Transformations: Translations, Reflections, and Rotations
concepts.description: Rigid transformations (isometries) preserve distance and angle measure. Translation: sliding every point the same direction and distance. Reflection: flipping over a line of symmetry. Rotation: turning around a fixed center point by a given angle. Coordinate rules for common transformations.

concepts.name: Dilations and Similarity Transformations
concepts.description: A dilation scales a figure by a scale factor k from a center of dilation. Dilation produces similar (not congruent) figures. The image coordinates: (kx, ky) for center at origin. Connecting dilations to proportionality and similar figures.

concepts.name: Two-Column and Paragraph Proofs
concepts.description: Structuring a deductive geometric proof using statements and reasons. Common reasons: definitions, postulates, theorems, properties of equality/congruence. Reading and writing two-column proofs and paragraph proofs. The role of axioms and theorems as logical foundations.
